blocks.content:
• Venus is hottest — NOT Mercury.
• Jupiter is largest.
• Saturn least dense.
• Uranus rotates sideways.
• Asteroid belt between Mars & Jupiter.
• Universe expanding (Red Shift).

items: Common Trap: Students often mistakenly mark Mercury as the hottest planet because it is closest to the Sun; Venus is actually the hottest.
Location Alert: Exams frequently test the position of the Asteroid Belt—remember it lies strictly between Mars and Jupiter.
Concept Alert: Red Shift is the specific astronomical term associated with the expansion of the Universe.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system, not Mercury.
Jupiter holds the distinction of being the largest planet.
Saturn has the lowest density of all planets.
Uranus features a unique sideways rotation.
The asteroid belt is situated between Mars and Jupiter.
Red Shift demonstrates that the Universe is continuously expanding.
